newsitem.title: INDIA: ANZ says not worried about takeover.
newsitem.headline: ANZ says not worried about takeover.

text.p: The Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (ANZ) Ltd is not worried about being a takeover target, ANZ's chief executive officer Don Mercer said on Monday.
Mercer, who is in the Indian capital for an ANZ board meeting, told Reuters: "We are not worried about a takeover."

He said an inquiry currently being made into Australia's financial system could result in an end to the policy laid down by former Australian Prime Minister Paul Keating which forbade mergers and takeovers among the country's "Big Four" banks and two major life insurers.
"You could well see a return to market conditions," Mercer said.
Stan Wallis, who chairs the financial system inquiry set up by Australian Treasurer Peter Costello, said earlier this month he expects his report to be ready on schedule by the end of March.

The inquiry has received submissions from the banking, financial and insurance sectors about changes to the regulatory framework, which now prevents mega-mergers between the major banks and life offices and also frowns on takeovers of the regional banks that specialise in home loans.
Analysts have pointed to the likelihood that National Australia Bank Ltd will launch a takeover of fellow "big four" bank Westpac Banking Corp once the Wallis report is handed down.
Mercer has cited good performance and a good share price as the best defences against takeover.
ANZ's cost-to-income ratio is the weakest of the four big banks at 67.3 percent.
Last November ANZ said net profit for the year to September 30, 1996 rose 6.7 percent to A$1.12 billion. It shares closed at A$8.29 on Monday.
